candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: protect clients and health care personnel from hazards; apply infection-prevention principles; promote staff and workplace safety
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — occupational infection exposure / measles work restriction
candidate.educational_objective: Apply CDC work-restriction guidance for measles-exposed health care personnel who lack presumptive evidence of immunity.

options.A: Exclude the worker from work from the 5th day after the first exposure through the 21st day after the last exposure, regardless of receipt of postexposure prophylaxis
options.B: Allow unrestricted work as long as postexposure prophylaxis is given
options.C: Exclude the worker only after a measles rash appears
options.D: Exclude the worker for exactly 48 hours after the exposure, then return without monitoring

candidate.rationale: CDC recommends that asymptomatic health care personnel without presumptive evidence of measles immunity who are exposed to measles receive appropriate postexposure prophylaxis and be excluded from work from the 5th day after their first exposure through the 21st day after their last exposure, regardless of receipt of PEP. Therefore A is correct. The other options would permit work during a period when a susceptible exposed worker could become infectious or use an unsupported duration.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Susceptible measles-exposed HCP should be excluded from work from day 5 after first exposure through day 21 after last exposure, even if postexposure prophylaxis is administered.
candidate.source_document_title: Measles — Infection Control in Healthcare Personnel
candidate.source_locator: Recommendations #2: asymptomatic HCP without presumptive evidence of measles immunity after exposure — administer PEP and exclude from work from day 5 after first exposure through day 21 after last exposure regardless of PEP

candidate.stem: An asymptomatic health care worker without presumptive evidence of measles immunity has an occupational measles exposure. Which work-restriction instruction is consistent with CDC guidance?
